rationale:
ROUND 7 of 7ba5b8c4 — SCOPE SPLIT, and the split is the substantive change.

Rounds 1-6 read: 5/3, 5/3, 8/2, 10/1, 6/4, 9/3. It stopped converging at round 4 and I can now say why. **Every one of round 6's six objections was about `recordIndexNote`, a helper I invented in round 6. Not one was about markdown indexing.** The core change has drawn no objection since round 4. What has been generating objections is a prune-safety sub-feature that ACCRETED IN RESPONSE TO REVIEW: bug_historian flagged the unguarded prune (round 3) -> I added a floor (round 4) -> the floor needed a durable surface (round 5) -> the surface needed a helper (round 6) -> the helper drew six objections. Each fix added mechanism and each new mechanism became fresh surface. That is a moving target, and continuing to iterate it inside this plan spends council rounds on a change that is not what this plan is for.

**The prune defect is PRE-EXISTING AND INDEPENDENT.** The shared prune has no floor for the Go-symbol rows TODAY, with or without markdown. bug_historian found it by reading my call site, not my change. It is now filed as **bugs_open/135**, carrying the design the six rounds produced -- the per-kind floor, the resolvable ratio (guardian: a guard with no exit is a defect in costume), the durable surface, and the HARD-WON negative result that site_work_items cannot be used (site_id/handler_agent/pipeline are NOT NULL; this indexer is repo-wide) so doc_notes is the fit. The next thread starts from the end of that argument.

WHAT THIS ROUND SUBMITS is therefore rounds 1-4's core, with the accretion removed: relax the kind CHECK, index markdown sections from four durable sources, per-glob counts with a zero-match glob failing the doc half only. **The prune behaviour is UNCHANGED from today** -- this plan no longer touches it. That is not a retreat from the safety concern; it is putting it where it can be fixed for the rows it actually endangers most, which are the code rows this plan does not add.

CARRIED FORWARD, all previously checked and still attached in grounded_in: docs/ is on disk (github_source.go:196-245 writes every tar entry, no path filter; the exclude at analyse_repo_local_action.go:285 is analyser-time) and out.Root survives collected_data (runtime: the 07-04 layer-1 run logged root=/tmp/analyser-src-451921075 files_read=543); the register glob is register/*.md (110 entries), not the parent (28 superseded planning docs) -- round 1's real defect; no reader switches on kind (re-checked round 6: one hit, resolved as the analyser's typeDef.Kind, not the table); no markdown splitter or parser exists to reuse (chunkContent is a fixed-width window; extractProductSection truncates at a marker list; goldmark is go.sum-graph-only, absent from go.mod, imported nowhere; the receiver-form blind spot in that search was closed in round 4).

SIZING, corrected in round 5 and stated plainly: **~3,472 sections against 4,992 code rows, +70%** -- not the ~1,749/+35% I quoted in rounds 1-4, which predated the register-glob fix and counted none of the 110 register files.

plan.summary: ROUND 7, SCOPE SPLIT. D11 layer 1b: relax the kind CHECK and index markdown sections from four durable prose sources into code_symbols, reusing layer 1's body column and content search. The prune-safety sub-feature that accreted across rounds 4-6 -- and which generated ALL of round 6's objections while the core drew none -- is removed and filed as bugs_open/135, because it guards a pre-existing exposure on the code rows independent of this change. Prune behaviour is unchanged from today.

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- the mechanical blocker. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. READERS enumerated for guardian (round 1, medium): no reader switches on kind; diagnose_code_lookup never selects it; scanCodeSymbolRows selects it into lookup_code_symbols' result map only. NUMBER MOVES -- 253 is highest today, but this workstream's last migration was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241 and 242 inside four hours. Re-read the max immediately before writing the file.

ROUND 2, answering debug_historian (medium): the needle-gate discipline wants verify AND rollback as separate files, and this constraint relaxation is what makes the Go writer's INSERTs possible at all -- so a bad flattenMarkdown run had no scripted recovery. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT TRIVIAL: the old CHECK cannot be restored while kind='doc' rows exist, so the rows must be deleted FIRST or the ALTER fails with a check-violation on existing data. Written as one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable.

ROUND 3, rewritten for bug_historian (medium): the round-2 guard fired only on a TOTAL of zero, and round 1's real defect was non-zero-but-wrong-source. Now: counts are tracked PER GLOB and returned; a glob matching ZERO FILES is a hard error (the plan's only fail-loud escalation, because a source contributing nothing is indistinguishable from a source that does not exist); and the scope/path-shape assertion runs HERE, every index, not only in a VERIFY a human runs once. NOT REUSING, with the search attached in the rationale: chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396) is a fixed-width window; extractProductSection (vet_med_price_scrape_action.go:650) is markdown- and heading-aware but TRUNCATES at a fixed end-marker list and returns one prefix with no spans; no markdown parser is a dependency (goldmark is go.sum-graph-only, absent from go.mod, imported nowhere). Suffix determinism, for guardian (low): the counter is a per-file map[string]int incremented during ONE top-to-bottom pass over the file's own lines, so the Nth occurrence gets the same suffix every run -- document order, never map iteration order.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. composeSymbolContent keeps the code BODY out for exactly this reason; markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only; the section text goes to body, which is what the content check now searches anyway.

ROUND 7: append markdown rows to the Go rows before the EXISTING upsert/prune loop, which is UNCHANGED by this plan. Round 4-6's prune floor is removed and filed as bugs_open/135 -- it guards a pre-existing exposure on the code rows that exists with or without this change, and iterating it here was spending council rounds on a different change. Prune behaviour after this plan is exactly what it is today. THE GLOBS ARE THE DESIGN and round 1 got one wrong: the register is register/*.md (110 entries), not the parent (28 superseded planning docs). Owning pipeline (attached, not asserted): agent code-indexer, step index_symbols, spawned by index-orchestrator, fired by scheduled task code-index-refresh every 86400s.

A SUPPLEMENT, not a fix -- explicitly conceding editquality (low, edit 6): this file changes no behaviour and is not counted as covering any mechanism. It exists because 243's VERIFY caught a real defect in layer 1 that a reviewer had been asked to eyeball. Carries the 243 lesson forward: that file's EXPLAIN stayed pinned to the OLD predicate after the code changed, so it reported on a query nobody ran while presenting as coverage -- these assertions must be re-read whenever flattenMarkdown or the globs change.

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT: content and content_hash must not gain section text or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only; the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows. (2) EMBEDDING COST: ~3,472 new rows each embed once on first index. Layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction; this is not, and it is stated. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: in-file duplicate headings measured at 1 today (WRONG_CALLS.md 212 headings / 211 unique); the suffix counter runs in document order over one top-to-bottom pass, so it is stable across runs. (4) SCOPE IS THE DESIGN AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG ONCE: the register glob pointed at 28 superseded planning docs instead of 110 register entries -- a wrong glob poisons the corpus with the stale-doc class this plan exists to keep out, while every counter reports success. Per-glob counts, a zero-match glob failing the doc half, and the VERIFY's out-of-scope + register_sections assertions are the guards. (5) BLAST RADIUS of the CHECK widening, enumerated and re-checked: no reader switches on kind; the only behavioural change is that a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k, which is the intended effect. (6) PRUNE: unchanged by this plan. The pre-existing no-floor exposure is bugs_open/135. (7) DEPLOY: Go is inert until the image rolls; the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break.
